newsitem.title: USA: Qualcomm, Sony introduce new digital phones.
newsitem.headline: Qualcomm, Sony introduce new digital phones.

text.p: Qualcomm Inc. and Sony Corp.'s U.S. Wirelss Telecom unit unveiled Monday a new generation of digital phones designed to handle calls over the newer, second generation of mobile phone networks known as Personal Communications Services (PCS).
Qualcomm and Sony are involved in a joint venture, Qualcom Personal Electronics, to build and market the phones. Qualcomm owns 51 percent and Sony the remaining 49 percent.
The new products are in contrast with the now widespread cellular networks based on older analogue technology.

In a bid to accelerate the transition to the new PCS-type networks, Qualcomm and Sony said some of the new models offer dual-mode capabilities allowing callers to use the phones on both new digital PCS and older analogue cellular networks.

The last six months have seen the rapid introduction of PCS networks, that when fully built will cover big portions of the United States. For now, regional coverage remains a patchwork of old and new.
Qualcomm, based in San Diego, Calif., said the new line-up includes a five-ounce "palm-sized" model that is the lightest digital cellular phone available.

The new phones are expected to be commercially available to both U.S. and overseas carriers this summer. A Sony official said the phones would range in price from $199 to $299 at retail stores in the United States.
